title: The Advantage of Speed
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This essay argues that organizations underestimate speed as a competitive differentiator, and that picking just one area to become genuinely best-in-class fast can produce outsized advantage. Using examples ranging from the SR-71 Blackbird's defensive reliance on pure velocity to consumer brands like Amazon, Uber, Zara, and Goldman Sachs, it illustrates how speed in a single dimension — delivery, pickup, market response, fashion cycles — can become a defining brand identity. The piece closes by urging leaders, regardless of company size, to identify one arena where world-class speed could set them apart.
points: Argues speed is an underrated competitive differentiator that most organizations don't deliberately invest in.
Recommends focusing speed investment on just one area rather than trying to be fast everywhere at once.
Uses the SR-71 Blackbird's reliance on pure velocity as a defense mechanism as a vivid illustration of speed as strategy.
Cites specific real companies (Amazon, Uber, Zara, Goldman Sachs) as examples of firms that built brand identity around speed in one dimension.
Frames the speed advantage as accessible to organizations of any size, not just large enterprises.
quotes: Organizations that figure out how to achieve a best-of-class speed in one or more areas of their enterprise have a big advantage over their industry peers or competitors.

High levels of speed allow organizations to capture opportunities faster than everyone else. Enterprises that move fast can capitalize on emerging trends and shifts in customer preferences better than others.

Look at the advantage the US military enjoys by emphasizing technological speed in its equipment. Consider the example of the SR-71 Blackbird jet, the fastest air-breathing manned aircraft that’s ever flown.

Some of the best organizations in the world have used speed to dominate their competitors. Well-known companies like Amazon (speed of delivery), Uber (speed to pick up), Apple (speed to market), Lufthansa (speed to dynamic ticket prices), Zara (speed to fashion design), and Walmart (speed to restock products) are just a few examples.

You don’t need to be a massive company to focus on the advantages of speed. Any organization can make speed in one arena a priority, design ways to achieve world-class speed, and benefit from the superior value that speed offers.
